title: The Battle Over the Democratic Party's Future

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日时事通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上，现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today's
sentences.zh: 今天的

sentences.en: Senate primary in Kentucky has been transformed by the outcry over police brutality.
sentences.zh: 肯塔基州参议院初选因对警察暴行的强烈抗议而发生了转变。

sentences.en: Jonathan Martin, on what the election can tell us about the future of Democratic politics.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·马丁将讲述这场选举能告诉我们关于民主党政治未来的什么信息。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月23日，星期二。

sentences.en: Jonathan, tell me about today's Senate race in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，跟我说说今天肯塔基州的参议院竞选吧。

sentences.en: Well, this is the Democratic primary to take on Senator Mitch McConnell, who of course is the majority leader of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是民主党初选，胜者将挑战参议员米奇·麦康奈尔，他当然是参议院的多数党领袖。

sentences.en: And for a long time, it seemed like his Democratic opponent was going to be Amy McGrath.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，他的民主党对手似乎会是艾米·麦格拉思。

sentences.en: I'm Amy McGrath, and I love our country.
sentences.zh: 我是艾米·麦格拉思，我热爱我们的国家。

sentences.en: I spent 20 years as a U.S.
sentences.zh: 我曾在美国海军陆战队服役20年，

sentences.en: Marine, flew
sentences.zh: 飞行了

sentences.en: 89 combat missions bombing Al-Qaeda and the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 89次战斗任务，轰炸基地组织和塔利班。

sentences.en: Who came to some fame nationally in her 2018 house race on the basis of her resume.
sentences.zh: 她在2018年的众议院竞选中凭借自己的履历在全国范围内获得了一些名气。

sentences.en: I was the first woman Marine to fly in an F-18 in combat, and I got to land on aircraft carriers.
sentences.zh: 我是第一位驾驶F-18战斗机执行战斗任务的女海军陆战队员，我有幸在航空母舰上降落。

sentences.en: She was a Marine pilot and entered the house race talking a lot about her military experience.
sentences.zh: 她曾是一名海军陆战队飞行员，在参加众议院竞选时，她谈论了很多自己的军事经历。

sentences.en: This is my new mission, to take on a Congress full of career politicians who treat the people of Kentucky like they're disposable.
sentences.zh: 这是我的新使命，去挑战一个充斥着职业政客的国会，他们对待肯塔基州人民就像对待一次性用品一样。

sentences.en: And almost immediately gain this national profile.
sentences.zh: 并且几乎立即获得了这种全国性的知名度。

sentences.en: Some are telling me a Democrat can't win that battle in Kentucky, that we can't take back our country for my kids and yours.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我，民主党人在肯塔基州赢不了那场战斗，我们无法为我的孩子和你们的孩子夺回我们的国家。

sentences.en: We'll see about that.
sentences.zh: 我们走着瞧。

sentences.en: But she was not a terribly good candidate, it turns out.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，她并不是一个非常出色的候选人。

sentences.en: So this is a disappointment to Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以这对民主党人来说是一个失望。

sentences.en: It comes from the state of Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 这来自肯塔基州。

sentences.en: Amy McGrath, the former Marine combat pilot, defeated by the four-term incumbent, Andy Barr.
sentences.zh: 前海军陆战队战斗机飞行员艾米·麦格拉思被四届连任的现任议员安迪·巴尔击败。

sentences.en: She was running in a pretty difficult seat for a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 她当时竞选的席位对民主党人来说相当困难。

sentences.en: But this is a district that Trump won by 15 points.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个特朗普以15个百分点优势获胜的选区。

sentences.en: Her opponent, Andy Barr, looks like we'll get that fourth term.
sentences.zh: 她的对手安迪·巴尔看起来将获得第四个任期。

sentences.en: And she lost in what was otherwise a great year for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而且她在民主党本应表现出色的一年里输掉了选举。

sentences.en: But Chuck Schumer, who runs the Senate Democratic Caucus and effectively runs recruitment of Senate Democratic candidates, figured that she had one very important
sentences.zh: 但负责参议院民主党核心小组并有效负责招募参议院民主党候选人的查克·舒默认为，她有一个非常重要的

sentences.en: asset that could help him in 2020.
sentences.zh: 资产可以帮助他在2020年获胜。

sentences.en: She raised a lot of money and built a large list of national donors in 2018.
sentences.zh: 她在2018年筹集了大量资金，并建立了一个庞大的全国捐赠者名单。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so as this Senate, not House race, gets underway this year, I'm guessing Chuck Schumer decides to look to Amy McGrath once again.
sentences.zh: 所以随着今年这场参议院竞选（而不是众议院竞选）的开始，我猜查克·舒默决定再次看向艾米·麦格拉思。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because the idea was not necessarily to beat Mitch
sentences.zh: 因为当时的想法不一定是击败米奇·

sentences.en: McConnell, but to at least keep the race competitive, keep McConnell pinned down in Kentucky, keep him
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔，而是至少要让竞选保持竞争力，让麦康奈尔被困在肯塔基州，让他

sentences.en: focused on raising money for his own re-election, and perhaps siphon some national GOP money that would otherwise go to different states and have it go to Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 专注于为自己的连任筹款，并可能从原本会流向其他州的全国性共和党资金中分流一部分到肯塔基州。

sentences.en: So that was Schumer's thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是舒默的想法。

sentences.en: Look, Amy McGrath is our candidate.
sentences.zh: 看，艾米·麦格拉思是我们的候选人。

sentences.en: She's a strong candidate.
sentences.zh: 她是一位强有力的候选人。

sentences.en: And he looked at McGrath and saw her money potential, saw the sort of breadth of her national donor list and said, she's giving McConnell a run for his money.
sentences.zh: 他看着麦格拉思，看到了她的资金潜力，看到了她全国捐赠者名单的广度，并说，她正在给麦康奈尔带来挑战。

sentences.en: The Republican super PAC put $10 million into Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 共和党超级政治行动委员会向肯塔基州投入了1000万美元。

sentences.en: She's doing very well.
sentences.zh: 她表现得非常好。

sentences.en: And this is who I want to be our nominee against
sentences.zh: 这就是我想要成为我们对抗

sentences.en: McConnell.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔的提名人选。

sentences.en: And I'm going to make sure that she does not have any kind of a consequential primary to speak of.
sentences.zh: 而且我要确保她不会遇到任何值得一提的竞争性初选。

sentences.en: So he wants to clear a path for her to become the nominee.
sentences.zh: 所以他想为她成为提名人扫清道路。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Schumer wants to clear the field.
sentences.zh: 舒默想清理赛场。

sentences.en: He wants McGrath to be their candidate.
sentences.zh: 他希望麦格拉思成为他们的候选人。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to deal with drama in the primary.
sentences.zh: 他不想在初选中处理任何戏剧性事件。

sentences.en: He just wants to have her raising money, putting up enormous numbers to spook McConnell and divert
sentences.zh: 他只想让她筹集资金，拿出惊人的数字来吓唬麦康奈尔，并转移

sentences.en: McConnell's attention back to his own home state and his own re-election.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔的注意力回到他自己的家乡州和他自己的连任竞选上。

sentences.en: So it does seem like for some time that McGrath is not going to have a terribly competitive primary.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来有一段时间麦格拉思不会遇到太激烈的初选。

sentences.en: And so while McGrath seems to be full steam ahead towards the general election with not much of a primary to speak of, she is banking money at an extraordinary rate.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然麦格拉思似乎正全速前进迈向大选，且几乎没有值得一提的初选，但她正在以惊人的速度筹集资金。

sentences.en: She has raised over $40 million, which is more money than a lot of candidates raise in an entire campaign, let alone a primary.
sentences.zh: 她已经筹集了超过4000万美元，这比许多候选人整个竞选周期筹集的资金还要多，更不用说初选了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: So as far as everybody is concerned, especially back in Washington,
sentences.zh: 所以就大家而言，特别是在华盛顿，

sentences.en: Amy McGrath is on a glide path to the nomination.
sentences.zh: 艾米·麦格拉思正处于获得提名的顺风车上。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And then something happens.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一些事情。

sentences.en: We turn now to a deadly police-involved shooting in Louisville.
sentences.zh: 我们现在转向路易斯维尔发生的一起致命的警察枪击事件。

sentences.en: The victim was an EMT.
sentences.zh: 受害者是一名急救医疗技术员（EMT）。

sentences.en: Her family claims she was executed by police as officers served a search warrant in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 她的家人声称，她在深夜警察执行搜查令时被警察处决了。

sentences.en: On March 13th, shortly after midnight, Louisville police officers used a battering ram to enter the
sentences.zh: 3月13日午夜过后不久，路易斯维尔警官使用破门锤进入了

sentences.en: apartment of Breonna Taylor, who was a 26-year-old African-American emergency room tech.
sentences.zh: 布雷奥娜·泰勒的公寓，她是一位26岁的非裔美国急诊室技术员。

sentences.en: And shot her eight times while she was in bed in her own apartment.
sentences.zh: 并在她躺在自己公寓的床上时向她开了八枪。

sentences.en: So they just went into her apartment looking for a suspect whom we now understand was already in police custody.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是进入她的公寓寻找一名嫌疑人，而我们现在了解到该嫌疑人当时已经在警方拘留中。

sentences.en: This is not unique to Louisville.
sentences.zh: 这在路易斯维尔并非个例。

sentences.en: This is- We need answers.
sentences.zh: 这是——我们需要答案。

sentences.en: We need answers because this should have never happened.
sentences.zh: 我们需要答案，因为这本不该发生。

sentences.en: And this killing of Ms. Taylor by Louisville police sparked an outcry in the state.
sentences.zh: 泰勒女士被路易斯维尔警察杀害一事在州内引发了强烈抗议。

sentences.en: We have a right to live while-
sentences.zh: 我们有权活着，而——

sentences.en: And how does that begin to impact this Senate race?
sentences.zh: 这开始如何影响这场参议院竞选？

sentences.en: The activism in the aftermath of the killing of Breonna Taylor and George Floyd is extremely intense in Kentucky and especially in Louisville.
sentences.zh: 在布雷奥娜·泰勒和乔治·弗洛伊德被杀后，肯塔基州尤其是路易斯维尔的激进主义活动极其强烈。

sentences.en: The demonstrations are nightly.
sentences.zh: 示威活动每晚都在进行。

sentences.en: There are clashes with police and there is a candidate who is running from Louisville.
sentences.zh: 与警察发生了冲突，而且有一位来自路易斯维尔的候选人正在参选。

sentences.en: He's an African-American and his candidacy is now starting to get more attention.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非裔美国人，他的候选资格现在开始受到更多关注。

sentences.en: I stand before you as your brother, as your cousin, as your neighbor, as your fellow good troublemaker.
sentences.zh: 我作为你们的兄弟、表亲、邻居、你们共同的优秀麻烦制造者站在你们面前。

sentences.en: My name is Charles Booker.
sentences.zh: 我的名字是查尔斯·布克。

sentences.en: 35-year-old state representative named Charles Booker.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫查尔斯·布克的35岁州众议员。

sentences.en: I am the state representative for the 43rd district, which we are standing in.
sentences.zh: 我是我们现在所处的第43选区的州众议员。

sentences.en: And if you are not from the 43rd district, I represent you anyway.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是来自第43选区，我也代表你。

sentences.en: So he represents what he likes to say is the poorest zip code in all of Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 所以他代表着他喜欢称之为肯塔基州最贫困的邮政编码区。

sentences.en: No one pays attention to my neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 没有人关注我的社区。

sentences.en: In the West End of Louisville with roughly 75,000 people, we have just a couple of grocery stores, a handful of dollar stores because they prey on us.
sentences.zh: 在路易斯维尔西区，大约有75000人，我们只有几家杂货店，几家一元店，因为他们掠夺我们。

sentences.en: He is from the West End of Louisville, black neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他来自路易斯维尔西区，一个黑人社区。

sentences.en: And if you need to use public transportation to get to the hospital, it can take you a couple of hours.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要乘坐公共交通工具去医院，可能需要几个小时。

sentences.en: Jobs have left.
sentences.zh: 工作机会已经流失。

sentences.en: And he is someone who is running as a progressive and had been running as a progressive.
sentences.zh: 他是一位以进步派身份参选的人，而且一直以进步派身份参选。

sentences.en: My platform is about ending structural inequity and ending generational poverty.
sentences.zh: 我的纲领是关于结束结构性不平等和结束代际贫困。

sentences.en: Talking about issues like the Green New Deal, like single-payer health care, but hadn't gotten a lot of attention in large part because he hadn't raised much money.
sentences.zh: 谈论像“绿色新政”、单一支付者医疗保健等议题，但没有得到太多关注，很大程度上是因为他没有筹集到多少资金。

sentences.en: And McGrath had raised so much cash.
sentences.zh: 而麦格拉思筹集了太多的现金。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But after the killing of Taylor and then Floyd.
sentences.zh: 但在泰勒和弗洛伊德被杀之后。

sentences.en: We are crying out for Breonna Taylor, but we're crying out for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们为布雷奥娜·泰勒哭泣，但我们也在为我们自己哭泣。

sentences.en: Once these demonstrations get going, there is now suddenly more attention to Booker because he is a state lawmaker who's in these protests.
sentences.zh: 一旦这些示威活动开始，现在突然有更多人关注布克，因为他是一位参与这些抗议活动的州立法者。

sentences.en: When Breonna died, when she was killed, a part of us was killed as well.
sentences.zh: 当布雷奥娜去世时，当她被杀时，我们的一部分也随之死去了。

sentences.en: He is getting tear gassed in the streets of Louisville and he is seeing this up front.
sentences.zh: 他在路易斯维尔的街头被催泪瓦斯袭击，他亲眼目睹了这一切。

sentences.en: And he's experiencing this himself, day in, day out in his hometown.
sentences.zh: 他自己也在家乡日复一日地经历着这一切。

sentences.en: He is effectively a Black Lives Matter candidate.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是一位“黑人的命也是命”候选人。

sentences.en: If you look like me, if you look like him, if you look like him, if you look like her, you may be seen as a deadly weapon before being seen as a human being.
sentences.zh: 如果你长得像我，如果你长得像他，如果你长得像他，如果你长得像她，你可能会在被视为人类之前先被视为致命武器。

sentences.en: It ain't right.
sentences.zh: 这不对。

sentences.en: And it's hurting all of us.
sentences.zh: 这伤害了我们所有人。

sentences.en: And so what happens to Booker's candidacy as these protests intensify in Louisville and all over the country?
sentences.zh: 那么，随着这些抗议活动在路易斯维尔和全国各地加剧，布克的候选资格会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, the two largest papers in the state, the Courier Journal in Louisville and Lexington Herald Leader, taking note of this fraught moment of racial politics,
sentences.zh: 嗯，该州最大的两家报纸，路易斯维尔的《信使日报》和《列克星敦先驱领袖报》，注意到了这个充满种族政治紧张的时刻，

sentences.en: endorse Booker and state that he's the best candidate for these times.
sentences.zh: 支持布克，并声明他是这个时代最好的候选人。

sentences.en: So that helps to give him traction.
sentences.zh: 这有助于给他带来动力。

sentences.en: And then, in addition to getting that key local support, he's getting the attention from national progressive leaders.
sentences.zh: 此外，除了获得关键的当地支持外，他还得到了全国进步派领导人的关注。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders offers his endorsement.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯提供了他的背书。

sentences.en: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez gets behind his candidacy.
sentences.zh: 亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯支持他的候选资格。
zh_words: 亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥

sentences.en: And that's putting him on the sort of national progressive radar screen, if you will.
sentences.zh: 这让他进入了全国进步派的视野，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, as Booker is, from everything you're describing, catching fire, what is the party's anointed candidate, Amy McGrath, doing in response?
sentences.zh: 那么，乔纳森，正如你所描述的一切，布克正在走红，党内指定的候选人艾米·麦格拉思对此有何反应？

sentences.en: Well, she is talking about these demonstrations and about the killing of George Floyd a little bit more in recognition that, you know, she can't take the primary for granted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她更多地谈论了这些示威活动和乔治·弗洛伊德被杀事件，认识到，你知道，她不能把初选视为理所当然。

sentences.en: But, you know, Amy McGrath is not a natural politician.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，艾米·麦格拉思不是一个天生的政客。

sentences.en: This was part of her struggle in 2018.
sentences.zh: 这是她2018年挣扎的一部分。

sentences.en: And it does not go perfectly when she tries to engage these issues.
sentences.zh: 当她试图参与这些议题时，情况并不完美。

sentences.en: In fact, in a debate, she's asked the question about...
sentences.zh: 事实上，在一次辩论中，她被问到了关于……的问题。

sentences.en: Have you been on the ground in Louisville with the protesters the last three days or in Lexington or elsewhere?
sentences.zh: 过去三天你是否在路易斯维尔与抗议者一起在现场，或者在列克星敦或其他地方？

sentences.en: Ms. McGrath.
sentences.zh: 麦格拉思女士。

sentences.en: Have you been to any of the protests?
sentences.zh: 你参加过任何抗议活动吗？

sentences.en: And she answers pretty awkwardly.
sentences.zh: 她的回答相当尴尬。

sentences.en: I have not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: And why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, I've been with my family and I've had some family things going on this past weekend.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我一直和我的家人在一起，上周末我家里发生了一些事情。

sentences.en: But I've been following the news and making sure that, you know, I think we're in the middle of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在关注新闻，并确保，你知道，我认为我们正处于大流行之中。

sentences.en: So suddenly, Amy McGrath's politics of moderation and her distance from these protests are seeming quite out of sync with the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，艾米·麦格拉思的温和派政治以及她与这些抗议活动的距离，似乎与当下完全脱节了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And more to the point, Booker is very much tapping into the moment.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，布克非常契合当下的时刻。

sentences.en: This is suddenly a competitive primary.
sentences.zh: 这突然变成了一场竞争激烈的初选。

sentences.en: Amy McGrath has had to spend an enormous amount of money on ads in the last couple of weeks to sustain her advantage.
sentences.zh: 艾米·麦格拉思在过去几周不得不花费巨额资金在广告上，以维持她的优势。

sentences.en: Money that I think she and National Democrats thought that they would use against McConnell.
sentences.zh: 我认为她和全国民主党人原本打算用这些钱来对抗麦康奈尔。

sentences.en: And Booker has made this more of a competitive race going into the primary Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 而布克让这场竞选在周二初选前变得更加激烈。

sentences.en: And so what is Booker's surge here?
sentences.zh: 那么布克在这里的激增意味着什么？

sentences.en: What does that mean for Democratic Party leaders back in Washington who bet so heavily on Amy McGrath?
sentences.zh: 这对华盛顿那些在艾米·麦格拉思身上押下重注的民主党领导人意味着什么？

sentences.en: So Booker illustrates that, you know, the intensity,
sentences.zh: 所以布克说明了，你知道，这种强度，

sentences.en: the activism that we're seeing on the streets of America in the last few weeks is now at the door front of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 我们在过去几周在美国街头看到的激进主义，现在已经来到了民主党的大门口。

sentences.en: And Democrats are eager to harness this energy and activism, especially when it comes to organizing against President Trump and the Republicans this fall.
sentences.zh: 民主党人渴望利用这种能量和激进主义，特别是在今年秋天组织反对特朗普总统和共和党人时。

sentences.en: But when it comes to their own races, their own primaries, their own party, it's more complicated.
sentences.zh: 但当涉及到他们自己的竞选、他们自己的初选、他们自己的党派时，情况就更复杂了。

sentences.en: So this does also represent a challenge to Democratic leaders.
sentences.zh: 所以这对民主党领导层来说也构成了一项挑战。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，去探索《纽约时报》呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 给你一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》的订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Jonathan, how is it a challenge for Democratic Party leaders to have a candidate like Booker doing really well?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，像布克这样表现出色的候选人，对民主党领导层来说怎么会是一种挑战呢？

sentences.en: Because on the surface, it seems like a hotly contested Democratic primary that raises lots of attention, raises lots of money, that that's a good thing for the party.
sentences.zh: 因为从表面上看，这似乎是一场竞争激烈的民主党初选，吸引了大量关注，筹集了大量资金，这对党派来说是件好事。

sentences.en: Well, it creates a challenge because Chuck Schumer has gotten used to being able to dictate primaries in the Senate races basically every two years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这之所以构成挑战，是因为查克·舒默已经习惯了在过去每两年一次的参议院竞选中掌控初选。

sentences.en: But it's not just about Schumer.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是关于舒默的问题。

sentences.en: This is about the Democratic Party's leadership being able to keep its grip on who the nominees are going to be, where the money is going to go.
sentences.zh: 这是关于民主党领导层能否继续掌控谁将成为候选人，以及资金流向何处的问题。

sentences.en: And this is a real challenge to that power, that grip on the party.
sentences.zh: 而这对那种权力，对那种党内掌控力来说，是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: And why does that grip matter if it's maybe out of sync with what Democratic primary voters want?
sentences.zh: 如果这种掌控力与民主党初选选民的意愿不符，那它为什么还那么重要呢？

sentences.en: Well, because leaders like Chuck Schumer and Nancy Pelosi believe that to keep or gain majorities, they have to appeal to a broad cross-section of voters.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为像查克·舒默和南希·佩洛西这样的领导人认为，为了保持或获得多数席位，他们必须吸引广泛的选民群体。

sentences.en: And that that means nominating some candidates who are more moderate depending upon the state or the district that they are running in.
sentences.zh: 这意味着根据他们竞选的州或选区，提名一些更温和的候选人。

sentences.en: And Booker does not fit that mold.
sentences.zh: 而布克并不符合那种模式。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Leaders like Schumer are skeptical that a candidate of Booker's liberal politics could win the race in a place like Kentucky where Trump won by 30 points four years ago.
sentences.zh: 像舒默这样的领导人怀疑，像布克这种自由派政治立场的候选人，能否在四年前特朗普以30个百分点优势获胜的肯塔基州赢得竞选。

sentences.en: But I think to get closer to the bone here,
sentences.zh: 但我认为要说到点子上了，

sentences.en: if Schumer is not able to control the outcomes of these Democratic primaries and he's got people in his caucus potentially who are not loyal to him,
sentences.zh: 如果舒默无法控制这些民主党初选的结果，而他的党团中又有一些可能对他并不忠诚的人，

sentences.en: who won despite his intervention, then that's going to create vote counting headaches for him.
sentences.zh: 那些不顾他的干预而获胜的人，那么这会给他带来计票上的头痛问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, looking at the map right now, his majority is probably going to be, if there is one, a seat or two.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，看看现在的选区图，如果他能保持多数席位，可能也就一两个席位。

sentences.en: It's not going to be that extensive.
sentences.zh: 不会有那么大的优势。

sentences.en: So every vote counts.
sentences.zh: 所以每一票都很重要。

sentences.en: So he's thinking about, who am I going to have in my caucus?
sentences.zh: 所以他在考虑，我的党团里会有谁？

sentences.en: Who's going to be reliable?
sentences.zh: 谁是可靠的？

sentences.en: Who's going to be less so?
sentences.zh: 谁又没那么可靠？

sentences.en: And that's where this matters.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题的关键所在。

sentences.en: This reminds me a little bit of what House Speaker Nancy Pelosi dealt with with the election of the squad, among whom is Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Rashida Tlaib,
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了一点众议院议长南希·佩洛西在处理“小分队”选举时的情况，其中包括亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯、拉希达·特莱布，
zh_words: 亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥

sentences.en: progressive Democrats who tugged the entire body at times to the left in ways that House leadership wasn't perhaps ready for.
sentences.zh: 这些进步派民主党人有时会将整个机构向左拉，而众议院领导层或许还没准备好应对这种局面。

sentences.en: But it's even more delicate in the case of Schumer because of math, because the Senate is going to be so closely divided next year.
sentences.zh: 但在舒默的情况下，情况更加微妙，因为数学上的原因，因为明年参议院的席位分配将非常接近。

sentences.en: And if Democrats have a majority, it'll be a narrow one.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党能获得多数席位，那也将是微弱的多数。

sentences.en: Think about it.
sentences.zh: 想想看。

sentences.en: Pelosi in the House, she won 40 seats in 2018.
sentences.zh: 佩洛西在众议院，她在2018年赢得了40个席位。

sentences.en: They had a pretty robust majority.
sentences.zh: 他们当时拥有相当稳固的多数席位。

sentences.en: So you could lose a handful of progressives like the squad and basically cater to your more moderate Democrats because those are the ones that had numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以失去少数像“小分队”那样的进步派，基本上迎合你更温和的民主党人，因为那些人占多数。

sentences.en: This is just a more sort of delicate situation because the Senate is on a knife's edge.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个更微妙的情况，因为参议院正处于刀尖之上。

sentences.en: Jonathan, we're talking about this race in Kentucky as if it is very high stakes for Chuck Schumer.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我们谈论肯塔基州的这场竞选，就好像它对查克·舒默来说利害攸关一样。

sentences.en: But how much does this race in particular really matter?
sentences.zh: 但这场竞选到底有多重要？

sentences.en: So this is less about eventually beating McConnell, which is going to be a tall order in Kentucky, than it is about what's happening in the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 所以这与其说是最终击败麦康奈尔（在肯塔基州这很难做到），不如说是关于民主党内部正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And it's not just in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是在肯塔基州。

sentences.en: Also on Tuesday, there is a competitive primary featuring Elliott Engel, who's the long-serving chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee,
sentences.zh: 同样在周二，有一场竞争激烈的初选，主角是长期担任众议院外交事务委员会主席的埃利奥特·恩格尔，

sentences.en: who's facing a primary from an African-American, Jamal Bowman.
sentences.zh: 他正面临来自非裔美国人贾马尔·鲍曼的初选挑战。

sentences.en: In Virginia, a fairly conservative district, there is also an African-American running in that primary.
sentences.zh: 在弗吉尼亚州一个相当保守的选区，也有一位非裔美国人参加初选。

sentences.en: So what I'm really interested in watching these primaries unfold is can progressives gather strength, organize,
sentences.zh: 所以我真正感兴趣的是观察这些初选的展开，进步派能否积聚力量、组织起来，

sentences.en: and sort of overcome the establishment candidates in some of these races?
sentences.zh: 并在其中一些竞选中战胜建制派候选人？

sentences.en: But also, is 2020 going to be, for black candidates, what 2018 was for a lot of women, which is sort of capturing the energy of the moment?
sentences.zh: 但同时，2020年对于黑人候选人来说，会不会像2018年对于许多女性一样，是那种抓住时代能量的时刻？

sentences.en: And I think that's going to be one of the most fascinating things to watch on Tuesday is can black candidates like Jamal Bowman in New York, like Booker in Kentucky,
sentences.zh: 我认为周二最引人注目的事情之一就是观察黑人候选人，比如纽约的贾马尔·鲍曼，肯塔基州的布克，

sentences.en: can they build these multiracial coalitions capitalizing on this extraordinary moment of race in America?
sentences.zh: 他们能否建立起这些多种族的联盟，利用美国这个非凡的种族时刻？

sentences.en: Jonathan, it would seem counterproductive, not to mention perhaps hypocritical,
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，民主党领导层阻碍你所描述的党内这种变革，似乎适得其反，更不用说可能有些虚伪了。

sentences.en: for the Democratic leadership to stand in the way of such a change within their party that you described.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，该党在2018年表示欢迎所有这些进步派女性，

sentences.en: I mean, the party said it welcomed all these progressive women in 2018,
sentences.zh: 难道它不应该在即将到来的选举周期中欢迎并庆祝非裔美国进步派候选人吗？

sentences.en: and wouldn't it want to welcome and celebrate African-American progressive candidates in this coming election cycle?
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题就在这里。

sentences.en: Well, here's the catch.
sentences.zh: 2018年民主党拥抱的许多女性其实更为温和。

sentences.en: A lot of the women in 2018 that Democrats embraced were more moderate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，“小分队”确实吸引了眼球，但2018年参选并获胜的许多不太出名的女性，在政治取向上要中立得多。

sentences.en: You know, the squad got the attention, but a lot of the women who ran and won in 2018 who were not as well-known are much more centrist in their political orientation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里的区别有两点。

sentences.en: I think the difference here is twofold.
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为人们担心他们的一些政治主张对于所在州或选区来说过于激进。

sentences.en: First of all, I think there's concern that some of their politics are too progressive for the states or districts.
sentences.zh: 其次，我认为在恩格尔众议员的案例中，这只是保护现任者的问题。

sentences.en: And I think in the case of Engel, of Congressman Engel, it's just a matter of protecting incumbents.
sentences.zh: 这是两党长期以来的规则，即支持现任者。

sentences.en: That's a longstanding rule in both parties, that they support incumbents.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，南希·佩洛西、安德鲁·科莫觉得有义务支持一位长期的盟友，一位正在寻求连任的人。

sentences.en: So, you know, Nancy Pelosi, Andrew Cuomo feel obliged to support a longtime ally, somebody who's up for re-election.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 他们不想失去忠诚的选票和长期的盟友。

sentences.en: They don't want to lose loyal votes, longtime allies.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，这对领导层来说都是有道理的。

sentences.en: That all makes sense for the leadership in theory.
sentences.zh: 但从非常实际的层面来看，民主党领导人更大的风险难道不是他们错失了这个时刻吗？

sentences.en: But isn't the greater risk for Democratic leaders on a really practical level that they are missing this moment?
sentences.zh: 他们没有支持这些候选人，他们冒着与这个在党内似乎正在崛起的强大选民群体失去联系的风险。

sentences.en: They are not getting behind candidates, and they risk losing touch with this very powerful constituency that seems to be ascendant within the party.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 左派会说，这就是当下的时刻，也是国家现在所需要和要求的。

sentences.en: The left would say, this is what the moment is, and this is what the country now needs and demands.
sentences.zh: 考虑到病毒、种族不公问题、经济崩溃，这个时刻呼唤美国进行真正实质性的、彻底的政策变革。

sentences.en: Given the virus, given the issues of racial injustice, given the economic collapse, the moment cries out for real substantive sweeping policy changes in America.
sentences.zh: 如果你不遵守这一点，如果你不认识到这一点，那么作为民主党领导人，你就脱离了群众。

sentences.en: And that if you don't abide that, if you don't recognize that, then you're out of touch as a Democratic leader.
sentences.zh: 我认为这场对话，左派与中间派在民主党内的这种紧张关系，真的会凸显出来。

sentences.en: And I think this conversation, this tension between the left and the center and the Democratic Party, I think is really going to come to the fore.
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下，乔纳森，我们最初关注的那些民主党领导人，比如舒默参议员，会怎么样？

sentences.en: And in that version of this, Jonathan, what becomes of some of these Democratic leaders who we started this conversation focusing on, like a Senator Schumer?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们必须适应这个时刻。

sentences.en: Well, they have to adapt to the moment.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不这样做，他们就会在自己的党内付出政治代价。

sentences.en: And if they don't, then they're going to pay a political price in their own party.
sentences.zh: 他们冒着失去对本党提名过程控制权的风险，因为他们会进一步助长左派的这种能量。

sentences.en: And they risk losing control of their own party's nominating process because they would further feed this energy on the left.
sentences.zh: 并冒着让自己的同事在初选中落败的风险。

sentences.en: And risk having their own colleagues lose primaries.
sentences.zh: 是的，甚至在舒默的情况下，他们还会冒着失去自己席位的风险。

sentences.en: And yes, even perhaps in Schumer's case, they would risk their own seats.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我花了很多时间与候选人交谈，他们经常试图回避，或者经常试图修饰他们的回答，以反映他们所竞选的州的情况。

sentences.en: You know, I've spent a lot of time talking to candidates, and they often try to hedge or they often try to trim their answers to reflect the states that they're running in.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我和布克交谈时情况并非如此。

sentences.en: Well, that was not the case when I talked to Booker.
sentences.zh: 艾米·麦格拉思，你的对手，你的初选对手，你认为她在秋季会输给麦康奈尔吗？

sentences.en: Amy McGrath, your opponent, your primary opponent, do you think that she would lose to McConnell on the fall?
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 他非常直率地表示，他认为那种温和的做法，试图不被视为真正的意识形态化，在肯塔基州是行不通的。

sentences.en: He was very straightforward about the fact that he believes the moderate approach, trying to not be seen as true ideological, was a loser in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 这是同样的剧本，每次都输。

sentences.en: It's the same playbook that loses every time.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种政治废话，说击败他们的唯一方法就是筹集一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And it's this political BS that says the only way you can beat them is just raise a whole lot of money.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 用广告轰炸电波。

sentences.en: Flood the airwaves.
sentences.zh: 不要谈论真正的问题。

sentences.en: Don't talk about real issues.
sentences.zh: 不要谈论贫困。

sentences.en: Don't talk about poverty.
sentences.zh: 只要玩政治游戏，你就能争取到一些保守派选民。

sentences.en: Just play the political game and you'll peel off some conservative voters.
sentences.zh: 那从来都不管用。

sentences.en: That never works.
sentences.zh: 但他说了，我们以前试过那个。

sentences.en: But he said we've tried that before.
sentences.zh: 他说我们一次又一次地看到那个剧本被使用，人们不会再上那种鬼话的当了。

sentences.en: He said we've seen that playbook used time and time again, and people are not going to fall for that bullshit again.
sentences.zh: 这些不是我出于政治经验而选择的问题。

sentences.en: These aren't issues that I'm choosing out of political experience.
sentences.zh: 这是出于生存的需要。

sentences.en: This is out of survival.
sentences.zh: 我们需要绿色新建筑，因为我们需要更清洁的环境。

sentences.en: We need a green new building because we need a cleaner environment.
sentences.zh: 我们需要可持续的工作岗位。

sentences.en: We need sustainable jobs.
sentences.zh: 我们需要在基础设施上进行更多投资。

sentences.en: We need more investment in our infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一个对自己忠诚的人，一个不会试图去敷衍或回避的人。

sentences.en: They want somebody who's going to be true to themselves, who is not going to try to sort of hammer or hedge.
sentences.zh: 他没有拐弯抹角。

sentences.en: And he didn't mean to any words.
sentences.zh: 但是查尔斯，当舒默在初选后的第二天给你打电话说，如果你想要钱，想要我们的帮助，你知道，

sentences.en: But Charles, what are you going to say the day after the primary when Schumer calls you on the phone and says, if you want the money, you want our help, you know,
sentences.zh: 你得在那些事情上放轻松点，你会怎么说？

sentences.en: you got to ease off on some of that stuff.
